To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We found behavioral evidence of top-down suppression of attention capture with the letter probe technique.
We used a modified additional single paradigm in which participants search for a target shape while ignoring a color singleton.

1) when participants were in singleton detection mode (i.e. they were searching for a color singleton) they showed behavioral evidence of top down attention capture (i.e. faster responses to probes at the singleton's location) 2) when participants were encouraged to search for the shape of a target, they showed no behavioral evidence of top-down attention capture 3) the finding of top down suppression in feature search mode is consistent with previous ERP evidence that shows suppression of early visual evoked responses
In summary, our research is concerned with
how visual attention is drawn to salient stimulus features.
understanding the nature of attentional capture.
the role of top-down control in attention capture by salient stimuli.
